items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: Milt doesn't get that kind of money.

ctx.x: That's interesting, because thre are classical musicians, and not only the very famous ones, the ones who are coming up, who get $10,000 a concert, but very few jazz people have ever done that.

No. He's a very dishonest man, and his wife -- he and his wife made millions of dollars off of hiring unknown musicians out in the sticks for little or no money, promise them one salary, get them out on the road and says, Lionel Hampton has the right to promise that kind of money. I was promised -- Lionel guaranteed me $400 a week when I first joined the band. And so I got on the road, I was very far away from California, and Hampton called to me and he says, why, we could pay that kind of money. No one -- Milt…
Gee, and you had to pay your other stuff besides.
